solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Copper pot briefly bugs artist

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, so POT loses its last letter

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot; POT cut short also gives PO
John Constable, the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: A policeman's pot is bugged by an artist, a picture of surveillance and petty mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like the metal of the pot, but it is slang for a police officer; the artist supplies the rank word in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A copper is British slang for a policeman, and a police constable is the basic rank.

clue.text: Horse uses gap to run free

explanation.surface: A horse slips through a gap in the fence and bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: The escaping horse is a real horse in the surface; the answer is the winged one of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegasus is the winged horse of Greek mythology.

clue.text: Belgian city's feudal lord

definitions.meaning: the French-speaking city on the Meuse in eastern Belgium
in the feudal system, the superior to whom a vassal swore allegiance

explanation.surface: A medieval lord rules over a Belgian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Liège is a Belgian city, and a liege is a feudal superior owed allegiance.

clue.text: Good to leave body in North America, perhaps

indicators.note: the G departs from the word

parts.note: a contingent is a body of people, such as troops

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to leave their body behind in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' suggests a physical body; here it is a group of people. G for good is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: North America is one example of a continent, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Head expelling one who does coursework?

parts.note: one = I, thrown out of CHIEF

explanation.surface: A head teacher expels a student who does coursework.
explanation.walkthrough: The school picture makes 'coursework' look like essays; a chef works on the courses of a meal. 'One' also serves the wordplay as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef prepares the courses of a meal, so does coursework in a punning sense.

clue.text: Imaginary number confused Latino

indicators.note: confused letters have lost their order, as a confused mind loses its thread

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A Latino person is baffled by an imaginary number in a maths lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imaginary number' is a phrase from mathematics, but the definition is 'Imaginary' alone and 'number' gives NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional means existing only as an idea, that is, imaginary.

clue.text: Bill with two zeroes added not acceptable

indicators.note: the zeroes are attached after the bill

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar

explanation.surface: A bill padded with two extra zeroes is not acceptable to the payer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is an inflated bill; the zeroes are letter O shapes rather than money.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is socially forbidden, not acceptable.

clue.text: Piece-by-piece analysis of failure

definitions.meaning: an itemised account splitting a whole into its parts
a collapse, as of a car, a machine or someone's health

explanation.surface: An inquiry dissects exactly why something failed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, an analysis of a failure, but it is two meanings joined by 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakdown is both a detailed analysis and a collapse or failure.

clue.text: Drones bombing base from the back

indicators.note: bombing wrecks the order of the letters

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Drones bomb an enemy base, attacking from the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the back' reads as a direction of attack, but 'back' is the definition, meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to publicly support a candidate or product.

clue.text: Rank in karate that can't be built upon?

definitions.meaning: a coloured-belt grade marking progress in martial arts
protected countryside ringing a British town, where development is barred

explanation.surface: A karate grade too lowly to build a career on.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the green belt is countryside ringing a city where building is restricted; the question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Green belt is both a karate grade and land protected from development.

clue.text: Cash raised for eavesdroppers

indicators.note: eavesdroppers only hear the word, so it is what it sounds like

parts.note: bred = raised, as children or livestock

explanation.surface: Money is collected to pay off people listening in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like fundraising alongside 'Cash'; it is the past tense of breed.
explanation.definitionFit: An old slang sense: money is what buys your daily bread, and dough works the same way.

clue.text: Consider appropriate charges to return it

indicators.note: the charges come back the other way

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper considers whether it is right to refund the charges on an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consider appropriate' is a verb phrase, matching the verb SEE FIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a set phrase for judging a course of action suitable, as in 'do as you think best'.

clue.text: Shrink admits lie exposed colleague

parts.note: to cower is to shrink back in fear
PORKY (rhyming slang: porky pie, lie) without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A therapist confesses that a colleague's lie was exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' tempts as a psychiatrist; it is the verb. A porky is British rhyming slang for a lie (porky pie). COW(ORK)ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who works alongside you in the same organisation.

clue.text: Ghosts from mouth of Styx facing the underworld

indicators.note: the mouth is the opening, the first letter

parts.note: S faces, stands in front of, the next piece

explanation.surface: Ghosts drift from the mouth of the river Styx into the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word fits Greek myth, so 'mouth' looks like a river mouth rather than the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades are the spirits of the dead in classical myth.

clue.text: Robot with gold fruit back from kitchen

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the tomato is botanically a fruit

indicators.note: the back of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A robot comes back from the kitchen carrying golden fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back from kitchen' reads as returning; it takes the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating machine, a robot.

clue.text: Tender bond breaks curse

parts.note: a bane is a curse or scourge

explanation.surface: A loving bond is enough to break a curse, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective for the bond; it is legal tender, money. BAN(KNOT)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A banknote is legal tender, money that must be accepted in payment.

clue.text: Position papers?

parts.note: reads as a stance on policy; the setter means a physical, specifically sexual, position
reads as official documents; here an ancient Indian treatise

explanation.surface: Policy documents setting out an official position.
explanation.walkthrough: A position paper is a policy statement; the question mark invites reading 'positions' as those described in the ancient Indian text.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kama Sutra is an ancient Indian text famous for describing sexual positions.

clue.text: Fanatic torn admitting iodine is something nourishing

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in fitness nut
rent = torn, as in a rent garment
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A health fanatic insists that iodine is nourishing.
explanation.walkthrough: NUT + R(I)ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: vitamins, minerals and proteins are substances the body draws nourishment from.

clue.text: Stop way of making subtitle subtle?

definitions.meaning: an informal command to quit doing something
remove IT from SUBTITLE and you get SUBTLE

explanation.surface: An editor asks how to make a film's subtitles less obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: SUBTITLE minus the letters IT is SUBTLE, so the instruction is literally 'cut IT out'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Cut it out' is an informal command to stop.

clue.text: Conventions area within airport?

definitions.meaning: the hall where arriving goods are checked for duty

explanation.surface: A conference centre tucked inside an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conventions' suggests conferences, matching the airport picture, but it means traditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs are social conventions and also the airport checkpoint for imported goods.

clue.text: Recompense guys covered in spots?

explanation.surface: A payout for men whose faces are covered in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' suggests acne; it means advertising slots. A(MEN)DS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: compensation offered to someone for a wrong done to them.

clue.text: Clip featuring live female animal

parts.note: to shear is to clip, as sheep
to be is to live, exist

explanation.surface: A video clip showing a live female animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clip' looks like a film clip; it is the verb, as in shearing wool. SHE(BE)AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: SHE marks the sex, as in she-wolf, attached to the animal itself.

clue.text: Boomers upset about king's headwear

indicators.note: the letters of BOOMERS are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: Baby boomers are angry about a king's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMB(R)ERO: the anagram of BOOMERS wraps the R. The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Red curio Jack smuggles

indicators.note: the words carry the answer hidden inside them

explanation.surface: A sailor named Jack smuggles a red curio through customs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a colour describing the curio; it is a red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish wine, most often red.

clue.text: Functional uniform with expensive fur

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A practical uniform trimmed with an expensive fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing, fitting the fur; it gives U.
explanation.definitionFit: Something usable is functional, fit for use.

clue.text: Youngster left Stairway to Heaven here?

explanation.surface: A young fan has left, playing the Led Zeppelin song 'Stairway to Heaven'.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title misdirects; the Tower of Babel was built to reach heaven, and the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tower of Babel was meant to reach the heavens, so it was a stairway to heaven of sorts.

clue.text: Menagerie evacuated twice for something viral?

indicators.note: emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters
the pair of letters is used two times

explanation.surface: A zoo is cleared out twice because of a viral outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viral' suggests disease in a zoo; the question mark points to internet virality.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is an idea or image that spreads rapidly online, going viral.

clue.text: Unfashionable hairstyle is better

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned haircut is somehow judged superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective; it is the verb, to surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with 'better' as a verb: to surpass someone's performance.

clue.text: Attractive to banish Democrat ready to get in

indicators.note: D is sent away from the word

parts.note: D = Democrat, removed from the front

explanation.surface: A charming candidate, ready to win office once the Democrat is ousted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attractive' looks like the definition, as a voter-friendly quality; it is the source word, and 'get in' means win an election.
explanation.definitionFit: An electable candidate is well placed to get in at an election.

clue.text: Legendary mariner astonished Blair at sea

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, the former prime minister, is amazed to meet a famous sailor out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the nautical picture perfectly while quietly meaning muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad the Sailor is the legendary seafarer of the Arabian Nights.
